title: A Quantitative Pólya--Szegő Theorem for Tangential Polygons
summary: For a bounded Lipschitz domain $Ω\subset\mathbb R^2$, let $T(Ω)=\int_Ωu_Ω\, dx$ denote its torsional rigidity, where $-Δu_Ω=1$ in $Ω$ and $u_Ω=0$ on $\partialΩ$. We prove a quantitative Pólya--Szegő inequality for tangential polygons. Let $N\ge3$, let $P$ be a tangential $N$-gon, set $A=|P|$, and let $R_N$ be the regular $N$-gon of area $A$. Writing $L(\cdot)$ for perimeter, we obtain the explicit deficit estimate \[ T(R_N)-T(P)\ge \frac{A^2}{8N\tan(π/N)} \left(1-\frac{L(R_N)^2}{L(P)^2}\right)^2.\]Thus, at fixed area, the torsional deficit is controlled from below purely by the perimeter…
